                ;**********************************************************************
                ; Purpose: Count two-bit selector use for an eight-row composite-image record and repeatedly discard the least-used eligible palette sources until enough standard slots are available. Inputs: $0E/$0F points at eight packed selector bytes, $0113-$011A holds their paired selector bytes, $0B-$0D maps three extra selectors, $33-$35 and $E3-$E6 describe candidate availability, $BC-$BE are standard-source eligibility guards, and $41 is the outstanding slot demand. Outputs: $39-$40 contains rebuilt use counts. Zero-use standard sources are marked in $33-$35; least-used eligible standard or extra sources are disabled through $33-$35/$E3-$E6, and $41 is decremented as mappings are released until the available-slot count satisfies it. Assumptions: Each of the eight rows supplies four valid two-bit selectors, selector and mapping indices are in range, and whenever more slots are required at least one eligible nonzero-use candidate exists. Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $22/$23, $33-$35, $39-$41, and $E3-$E6; $0B-$0D and $BC-$BE are read but preserved. Hardware changes: None; the routine only rewrites RAM palette-selection state consumed later by the image renderer.
                ;**********************************************************************

                ;**********************************************************************
                ; Purpose: configure the KERNAL logical-file parameters used by subsequent OPEN, LOAD, or SAVE calls. Inputs: A is the logical file number, X is the device number, and Y is the secondary address; Y=$FF means no secondary address. Outputs: KERNAL current-file variables receive A/X/Y. Assumptions: KERNAL ROM is banked in and this logical jump-table alias resolves to SETLFS at $FFBA. Clobbers: none; the documented SETLFS stores preserve A, X, Y, and flags. Hardware changes: none directly; it only prepares KERNAL RAM state for later device I/O.
                ;**********************************************************************
                ;**********************************************************************
                ; [offcut KERNAL_ROM::ffbd] Purpose: configure the KERNAL filename descriptor used by subsequent OPEN, LOAD, or SAVE calls. Inputs: A is the filename length and X:Y is the little-endian address of the filename bytes. Outputs: KERNAL filename length and pointer variables receive A and X:Y. Assumptions: KERNAL ROM is banked in and this logical jump-table alias resolves to SETNAM at $FFBD; the named byte range remains readable. Clobbers: none; the documented SETNAM stores preserve A, X, Y, and flags. Hardware changes: none directly; it only prepares KERNAL RAM state for later device I/O.
                ;**********************************************************************
                ;**********************************************************************
                ; [offcut KERNAL_ROM::ffc0] Purpose: open the logical file previously described by SETLFS and SETNAM. Inputs: KERNAL logical-file, device, secondary-address, and filename variables are initialized. Outputs: installs the open file in KERNAL file/device/secondary-address tables; carry is clear on success, while KERNAL errors return carry set with an error code in A. Assumptions: KERNAL ROM is banked in, the device is available, and this logical jump-table alias resolves through IOPEN at $031A. Clobbers: A, X, Y, and flags are volatile across device-specific OPEN processing; KERNAL file and I/O workspace changes. Hardware changes: may command the serial bus, cassette, or RS-232 hardware according to the selected device.
                ;**********************************************************************
                ;**********************************************************************
                ; [offcut KERNAL_ROM::ffc3] Purpose: close one KERNAL logical file and release or flush its device-specific state. Inputs: A is the logical file number previously opened. Outputs: removes that file from the KERNAL logical-file/device/secondary-address tables; device-specific completion may flush buffered output. Assumptions: KERNAL ROM is banked in and this logical jump-table alias resolves through ICLOSE at $031C. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, KERNAL file tables, and device workspace are volatile. Hardware changes: may send serial UNLISTEN, flush cassette output, or release RS-232 buffers according to the file's device.
                ;**********************************************************************
                ;**********************************************************************
                ; [offcut KERNAL_ROM::ffc6] Purpose: select an already-open logical file as the current KERNAL input channel. Inputs: X is the logical file number. Outputs: current logical file, device, and secondary address are selected; carry is clear on success, while lookup/device errors return carry set with an error code in A. Assumptions: the file was opened, KERNAL ROM is banked in, and this logical jump-table alias resolves through ICHKIN at $031E. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and KERNAL channel/serial workspace are volatile. Hardware changes: for serial devices, may issue TALK and a secondary-address command; otherwise updates software channel state.
                ;**********************************************************************
